decisions.reason: As a cutting and creasing finisher close to the core postpress range and already established on its own product page, it still fits the firm's automation-led portfolio and is unlikely to be withdrawn.

Although UV spot varnishing is somewhat farther from the traditional core, the firm treated it as a Germany-premiere flagship and it supports the strategic move into higher-value digital finishing, so continued support is more likely than withdrawal.
The sheet preparation module builds directly on the existing finishing workflow and modular automation offer, making it a natural product to retain in a growing market.
The B2-format multifinisher is both close to the established business and prominently highlighted as a focus product, so dropping it soon would run against the firm's stated direction.
A hybrid saddle stitcher sits firmly within the firm's booklet-making and binding competence and broadens a core category that customers regularly demand.
The folding add-on unit was marketed less prominently, but its documented customer installation and role as a modular extension to existing systems make retention more likely than exit.
